City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, September 19, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. 2023 SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS UPDATE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1) Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of September 5, 2023.
  2) Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of September 5, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – AUGUST 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-24 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for August 2023.

  D. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF AUGUST 31, 2023

  This report provides a fiscal year 2023-24 budget update for the City’s general
  fund as of August 31, 2023. The budget update incorporates the actual
  revenue received and expenditures that have occurred through August 31,
  2023, and projects the financial results for the year ending on June 30, 2024.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. APPROPRIATION REQUEST IN THE AMOUNT OF $131,750.56 FOR THE
  POLICE DEPARTMENT OFFICE SPACE ADDITION REQUEST

  In April 2022, construction began on the office space addition project at the
  Police Department. The completed project will provide much needed working
  space for Staff to continue serving the community. The funds budgeted for

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023  3
   this project have been exhausted. Additional funding is needed to complete
  the construction as well as furnishing the additional offices. Staff is requesting
  $100,000 to complete the construction of additional office spaces, and an
  additional $31,750.56 for furnishings for a total cost of $131,750.56.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1) Authorize the additional $100,000 funding to complete the Police Office
  Space Addition Project from the Development Impact Fund for FY 23-24;

  2) Authorize the use of the Omnia Public Sector Cooperative Agreement
  Region 4 ESC Contract #R191817 awarded to Trendway Design Studio to
  purchase modular office furniture in the amount of $18,872.64 from the
  Development Impact Fund for FY 23-24;

  3) Authorize the use of the Omnia Public Sector Cooperative Agreement
  Region 4 ESC Contract #R191817 awarded to 9to5 Seating to purchase
  office chairs in the amount of $12,877.92 from the Development Impact
  Fund for FY23-24;

  4) Adopt Resolution No. 23-54 to appropriate the additional $131,750.56 to
  the budget; and

  5) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute all agreements on
  behalf of the City.

  F. PURCHASE OF A FIRE DEPARTMENT COMMAND VEHICLE IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $213,930.19 AND UPFIT OF UTILITY TRUCK IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $53,561.66

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is in need of replacing its Front-Line
  Command Vehicle and to upfit a Utility Truck. The total purchase price of the
  Command Vehicle, including chassis, upfitting, tax and delivery, is
  $213,930.19. The total amount for the Utility Vehicle (chassis previously
  purchased) upfit, including tax and delivery is $53,561.66. The FY 2023-24
  adopted Fleet Service Fund budget included $160,000 for the purchase of the
  Command Vehicle (account 124-761-37-99-767). Appropriations are
  requested to be increased in the Fleet Services Fund in the amount of
  $107,491.85 to fund the total purchase amount of $267,491.85. The purchases
  are made with Sourcewell Contract 091521-NAF in compliance with Title III,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023  4
   Section 34.35 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, permitting the City to
  piggyback on a contract or cooperative purchasing agreement prepared by
  and processed through another local, state, or federal government agency.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-57 and
  authorize the issuance of purchase orders in the amount of $213,930.19 and
  $53,561.66 to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of a Command
  Vehicle and Utility Vehicle Uplift under Sourcewell Contract 091521-NAF as
  detailed in the staff report.

  G. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82176, A 4-UNIT
  CONDOMINIUM DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 117 WEST
  NORWOOD PLACE

  The development project located at 117 West Norwood Place, is a 4-unit
  condominium on a 16,000-square-foot lot. Staff and the City’s contract
  consultant for land surveying, RKA Consulting Group, Inc. have reviewed the
  Final Tract Map and determined that it is in compliance with the State
  Subdivision Map Act, Conditions of Approval, and the City’s ordinances
  regarding subdivision. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332. Class 32
  exemption (In-fill Development). The Planning Commission approved the
  project on January 14, 2029. In compliance with Section 66412.3 of the
  Subdivision Map Act, the Planning Commission has determined that the
  subdivision is consistent with the City’s actions with regards to the region’s
  housing needs.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Final Parcel Map No. 82176,
  authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  H. APPROPRIATION REQUEST FOR  CONTRACT  BUILDING  OFFICIAL
  TEMPORARY BUILDING SERVICES

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023  5
   Due to a temporary staffing shortage, the City is in need of additional building
  services to maintain an uninterrupted level of service in the Building Division.
  In August of this year, an emergency agreement was executed to onboard a
  contract Building Official. To date, the contract Building Official has been
  working with staff and project teams to see that construction and permits
  move forward. To maintain our level of service, the Department is requesting
  additional funding to maintain the temporary building services through this
  year. Funding for the services will be from the General Contractual Services
  Fund (121-810-16-22-000) in the amount of $40,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1) Adopt Resolution No. 23-56, increasing appropriations by $40,000 in the
  general fund for the costs of temporary building official services.

  2) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute an agreement with
  VCA Code Group to provide building official services.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AUTHORIZATION TO EXECUTE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH FAIRBANK, MASLIN, MAULLIN, METZ & ASSOCIATES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF UP TO $37,000 FOR A PUBLIC OPINION POLLING SERVICE
  REGARDING A PUBLIC SAFETY HEADQUARTERS POTENTIAL PROPERTY
  TAX INITIATIVE

  The City of San Gabriel’s Police Department Headquarters can no longer
  accommodate the staffing needs of its growing personnel nor support modern
  technological needs. The building is deteriorating and a remodel to bring the
  building to modern standards would be cost-prohibitive. Staff is seeking City
  Council’s approval to engage with a professional polling firm to conduct a
  comprehensive public opinion poll regarding an ad valorem tax initiative
  aimed to fund a new public safety headquarters that can serve as a single
  unified command center for both San Gabriel Police Department and San

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 19, 2023  6
   Gabriel Fire Department, to accommodate future growth needs and to
  continue to best serve the city’s residents and business community. Funds to
  conduct a public opinion survey are included in the fiscal-year 2023-2024
  general fund budget. The proposed cost for FM3 Research to perform a public
  opinion survey is up to $37,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Based on the submitted proposals’ polling strategies, past success, familiarity
  and experiences with the San Gabriel community, references, and
  recommendations from the strategic consultant, staff is recommending that
  the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with
  FM3 for a public opinion poll.

  B. COMMUNITY SERVICES / MISSION PLAYHOUSE UPDATE

  This is a presentation only; there is no staff report for this item.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 3, 2023 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 19, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:30 P.tvl. on Tuesday, September 19, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, Cal iforn ia, 91776, and announced that Council Member Ding
  was unable to attend the meeting.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor John Wu, and
  Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  Tony Ding.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney

I  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director
  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Publ ic
  Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Commun ity
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edwa rd El iza lde, Fire Division Chief Bradley Davis, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Special City Council Meeting of September 19, 2023 :

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION
  (GOVERNM ENT CODE §54956.9 [d] (21) (ONE CASE)

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that no reportable action was
  taken.

I  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved .

  CITY COUNCIL REGU LAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  September 19, 2023
   2. PRESENTATIONS

  A.  2023 SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS UPDATE

  San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments Administrative Services Manager Katie
  Ward made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

I  Michael Shutz, resident, provided comments in opposition to giving taxpayer funds to
  the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce and expressed his opinion that Mayor
  Harrington has a conflict-of-interest in this matter.

  Sonia Martin provided comments in favor of the City helping the San Gabriel Chamber
  of Commerce after getting more financial information and expressed disagreement
  with statements made by Mayor Harrington on the subject at a recent City Council
  meeting.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident and Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission Chair, provided comments expressing disappointment with the treatment
  of the indigenous community's input on Smith Park proposed changes and Mayor
  Harrington's participation in the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce membership
  consideration; and questioning the methodology for non-profit participation in City
  events.

  Cheryl Cabot, resident, provided comments objecting to Mayor Harrington's
  characterization of her articles regarding the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce, and
  commenting on related public records act requests and the Mayor's alleged conflict-

I  of-interest in the matter.
  Sam Guo, resident, commented about a parking ticket he received while transporting
  a disabled person and the lack of handicapped -parking spaces.

  Li Ping Chen commented on her experience as the handicapped person in the event
  described by Sam Guo and requested that the parking ticket fine be waived.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark noted that on item 4A, the dates in the footers of the Minutes
  had been corrected.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu, to
  approve Consent Calendar Item 4A as corrected and Items 4B - 4H as presented .

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 -0- 1 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON

I
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  DING

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of September 5, 2023.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of September 5, 2023 .

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  September 19, 2023
   B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved August 25, 2023, and August 31 , 2023, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - AUGUST 2023

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for August
  2023 .

I  D. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF AUGUST 31, 2023

  The City Council received and filed the report.

  E. APPROPRIATION REQUEST IN THE AMOUNT OF $131,750.56 FOR THE POLICE
  DEPARTMENT OFFICE SPACE ADDITION REQUEST

  The City Council :

  1) Authorized the additiona l $100,000 funding to complete the Police Office Space
  Add it ion Project from the Development Impact Fund for FY 23 -24;

  2) Authorized the use of the Omnia Public Sector Cooperative Agreement Reg ion
  4 ESC Contract #R191817 awarded to Trendway Design Stud io to purchase
  modular office furn iture in the amount of $18,872.64 from the Development
  Impact Fund for FY 23 -24;

  3) Authorized the use of the Omnia Public Sector Cooperative Agreement Reg ion
  4 ESC Contract #R191817 awarded to 9to5 Seating to purchase office chairs in

I  the amount of $12,877.92 from the Development Impact Fund for FY23 -24;

  4) Adopted Resolution No. 23-54 to appropriate the additional $13 1,750.56 to
  the budget; and

  5) Authorized the City Manager, or designee, to execute all agreements on behalf
  of the City.

  F. PURCHASE OF A FIRE DEPARTMENT COMMAND VEHICLE IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $213,930.19 AND UPFIT OF UTILITY TRUCK IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $53,561.66

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-57 and authorized the issuance of
  purchase orders in the amount of $213,930.19 and $53,561 .66 to Nationa l Auto
  Fleet Group for the purchase of a Command Vehicle and Utility Veh icle Uplift under
  Sourcewell Contract 091521 -NAF.

  G. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82176, A 4-UNIT CONDOMINIUM
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 117 WEST NORWOOD PLACE

I  The City Council approved Final Parcel Map No. 82176, authorized its filing with
  the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorized the City Manager to execute t he
  Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  H. APPROPRIATION  REQUEST  FOR  CONTRACT  BUILDING  OFFICIAL
  TEMPORARY BUILDING SERVICES

  The City Council:

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  Sept ember 19, 2023
   1) Adopted Resolution No. 23-56, increasing appropriations by $40,000 in the
  general fund for the costs of temporary building official services.

  2) Authorized the City Manager, or designee, to execute an agreement with VCA
  Code Group to provide building official services.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - NONE

I  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AUTHORIZATION TO EXECUTE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  FAIRBANK, MASLIN, MAULLIN, METZ & ASSOCIATES IN THE AMOUNT OF UP
  TO $37,000 FOR A PUBLIC OPINION POLLING SERVICE REGARDING A PUBLIC
  SAFETY HEADQUARTERS POTENTIAL PROPERTY TAX INITIATIVE

  Public Information Officer Clara Tsang made the presentation.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, provided comments in opposition to the
  agreement.

  Carina Rivera, resident, provided comments in favor of the agreement.

  Andrew, resident, questioned the choice of consultant, services provided for the
  cost, and where the money from Transit-Occupancy Tax and Measure SG is being
  used, and commented on employee salaries.

I
  Discussion included how the recommended consultant was chosen; details of a
  prior agreement with consultant FM3; how Measure SG funds are being used; the
  need for a dedicated funding source for a new public safety facility; community
  surveys that indicate the community's priority for public safety; methodology for
  the proposed survey and uses for the information that will be received; the
  deteriorating conditions of existing public safety facilities and their inadequacy to
  meet current and future needs; methodology for the languages to be supported
  for the poll and consultant capability for languages; poll focus on registered voters
  who will likely vote in the November 2024 election; contact methods for reaching
  respondents; benefits of a general obligation bond to fund a public safety facility;
  criteria to pass a special tax as opposed to a general tax; estimated cost to add a
  measure to the ballot; the poll as a tool to determine best timing for a ballot
  measure; rising construction costs; the need to accommodate adequate
  technology in a facility; and the benefits of using the expertise of a consultant.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with FM3 for a public
  opinion poll.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 -0- 1 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  DING

  B. COMMUNITY SERVICES/ MISSION PLAYHOUSE UPDATE

  Community Services Director Perez made the presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  September 19, 2023
   Andrew, resident, commented that there is not much activity for junior high and
  high school youth and advocated for youth ambassadors on the Community
  Services Commission.

  Discussion included ideas for a seating campaign to replace seats in the Mission
  Playhouse; progress toward a non-profit Community Foundation or 501 (c)(3) to
  accept donations; shortfall in the Mission Playhouse budget that is made up by the
  General Fund; improvements needed for the Playhouse; ability for the City to

I  produce Playhouse programming with greater funding; suggestions for changing
  programming; limitations on renovations to the Playhouse as a registered historic
  building; potential Lantern Festival event; RideSG program update; and Community
  Services Department staffing levels.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Ashley Sanchez requested a selfie with the City Council for a school assignment.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto reported that the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector
  Control District had notified the City of the first positive test for West Nile Virus in San
  Gabriel and reminded community to empty out standing water.

  Council Member Menchaca, as the City's representative to the Mosquito and Vector
  Control District, commented on resources available from the District.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

I  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at the San Gabriel employee health
  fair and thanked staff for coordinating it.

  Council Member Menchaca thanked Vice Mayor Wu and Council Member Ding for
  attending the 911 Memorial at Fire Station 51 and congratulated ColoradoBlvd .net on
  celebrating its 10th anniversary.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:41 P.M

  Respectfully submitted:

I
  Approved this 3rd day of October, 2023 :
